podEn: BG2Pod with Bill Gurley & Brad Gerstner
tEn: The AI Factory: The Heart of the AI Revolution
tZh: AI 工厂：AI 革命的核心
sEn: Jensen Huang explains how AI factories are driving the largest infrastructure buildout in history and why they are the best investment for enterprises in the next decade.
sZh: 黄仁勋解析 AI 工厂如何推动人类史上最大规模的基础设施建设，以及为何它们是企业未来十年的最佳投资。

consensus.en: AI evolved from generative chatbots to agentic systems that reason and do useful work, becoming economically valuable.
consensus.zh: AI已从生成式聊天机器人进化为能推理、做有用工作的智能体系统，具有经济价值。

consensus.en: Computing shifts from retrieval-based to generation-based, where every output is originally generated in real time.
consensus.zh: 计算正从基于检索转向基于生成，每个输出都是实时原创的。

consensus.en: AI factories—massive GPU clusters—produce intelligence tokens, representing a multi-trillion-dollar investment opportunity.
consensus.zh: AI工厂（大规模GPU集群）生产智能token，是数万亿美元的投资机会。

consensus.en: The AI industry is a five-layer cake: energy, chips, infrastructure, models, applications—each layer offers immense opportunity.
consensus.zh: AI产业是五层蛋糕：能源、芯片、基础设施、模型、应用——每层都蕴含巨大机遇。

consensus.en: AI won't eliminate jobs; it elevates them by automating tasks, letting people focus on purpose like design and problem-solving.
consensus.zh: AI不会消灭工作，而是通过自动化任务提升工作，让人们专注于设计、解决问题等目的。

consensus.en: AI will close the technology divide by letting everyone program computers via natural language, not just elite coders.
consensus.zh: AI将通过自然语言让每个人都能编程计算机，从而弥合技术鸿沟，而不再是精英程序员的专利。

contrarian.en: Contrary to fears, AI creates more jobs; radiology and software engineering jobs grew with AI augmentation, not shrank.
contrarian.zh: 与担忧相反，AI创造了更多就业；放射科和软件工程岗位因AI增强而增加，并未萎缩。

contrarian.en: Claims that AI might destroy humanity or is mysterious are nonsense; we understand it and make it safer each year.
contrarian.zh: 声称AI可能毁灭人类或神秘莫测是无稽之谈；我们理解它且每年都让它更安全。

contrarian.en: You won't lose your job to AI, but to someone who uses AI; therefore, everyone must engage with AI.
contrarian.zh: 你不会被AI取代，但会被使用AI的人取代；因此每个人都必须拥抱AI。

contrarian.en: The 80-trillion-dollar physical industries are AI's most important frontier, far beyond just language models.
contrarian.zh: 价值80万亿美元的物理产业才是AI最重要的前沿，远不止语言模型。

contrarian.en: Investing in sustainable energy for AI is the greatest opportunity in generations, reviving the energy sector.
contrarian.zh: 投资于AI所需的可持续能源是几代人最大的机遇，将重振能源行业。

contrarian.en: The claim that 90% of coding will vanish is naive; software engineers solve problems, not just type code.
contrarian.zh: 声称90%编程将消失是幼稚的；软件工程师的工作是解决问题，而非仅仅是敲代码。

transcript.sec: Opening Question: The AI Factory Investment

turns.en: Thank you so much, Jensen. So, we are in the middle of a massive AI revolution. It is probably bigger and faster than even the Industrial Revolution. And you have called out what's happening right now as the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. At the center of that buildout is the AI factory. And the company enabling all of that is Nvidia. Can you tell us what is an AI factory and why is it the best investment for any enterprise in the next decade?
turns.zh: 非常感谢你，Jensen。我们正处于一场大规模的 AI 革命之中，它可能比工业革命还要更大、更快。你称目前正在发生的是人类历史上最大的基础设施建设，而这其中核心就是 AI 工厂。促成这一切的公司正是 Nvidia。你能告诉我们什么是 AI 工厂，以及为什么它是未来十年所有企业的最佳投资吗？

turns.en: Okay, so you could understand AI in a particular number of ways. The way that you understand AI probably most is through a chatbot, through a web browser. You're interacting with it. You give it a prompt, it says something back to you. And even those of you who have been using AI for some time, you've seen in the last couple of two, three years a very significant evolution, improvement in the capabilities of AI. Two years ago, you heard about ChatGPT. ChatGPT basically is a computer software that understands the input you give it. It can perceive, understand information. And it can translate and generate the information into something else. Okay, so you can give it a prompt and you can say, 'Here's this PDF I gave you. I would like you now to summarize it.' It went from text to text. You could also tell it, 'Here's a PDF I gave you. I would like you to now generate an image of that story.' It would go text to image. You could use go from image to text, meaning you could give it a picture and you can say 'What's happening inside this picture?' It goes image to text. Does that make sense? Anything to anything else. AI in the last 2 years, 2 years ago was largely able to do this translation. We called it generation, generative models, okay? Generative AI. But the thing that is very big deal inside that word generative AI is in order to do something even more valuable than generation for understanding and generating is thinking. Well, you can't think if you don't generate words. And so the foundation of generative AI gave us the ability to generate internal thoughts. Thinking, reasoning, step-by-step reasoning, problem-solving. It also allowed us to do another thing that is now very important, which is generate intelligence to control something else. To generate control to use a tool. Does that make sense? To use a browser, use a spreadsheet, use Photoshop, use PowerPoint, use something, use AutoCAD, use another tool. Now, that tool today is digital, but someday that tool will be mechanical. So, if I generate a command to a mechanical system, that would be called robotics. If I generate commands for a machine with a steering wheel, that would be called self-driving cars. Does that make sense? Okay. So 2 years ago, in fact, you saw the foundations, we call it ChatGPT, and everybody said, 'You know, it's fun. It's silly.' Or it produced a whole bunch of crazy hallucinated text. That's all true, but it was the foundational technology that led to all of this. 2 years later, we now have agentic systems. Now, that's one view of AI. I just described the view, which is what can AI do?
turns.zh: 好的，你可以从几个方面来理解 AI。最常见的方式是通过聊天机器人、通过浏览器。你和它交互，给出提示，它回复你。即使是那些使用 AI 有一段时间的人，在过去两三年里也看到了 AI 能力的显著进步。两年前，你听说了 ChatGPT。ChatGPT 基本上是一个能理解你输入的计算机软件。它可以感知、理解信息，并能将信息转换并生成成另一种形式。比如，你可以给它一个提示：“这是我给你的 PDF，请你总结一下。”它实现了从文本到文本。你也可以说：“这是我给你的 PDF，请你为这个故事生成一张图片。”它就实现了从文本到图像。你也可以从图像到文本，也就是给它一张图片问：“这张图片里发生了什么？”它就实现从图像到文本。明白吗？任何形式到任何形式。两年前的 AI 大体上能做这种转换，我们称之为生成，生成式模型，也就是生成式 AI。但生成式 AI 这个词里非常重要的一点是，要想做比理解和生成更有价值的事——也就是思考——你就得先生成词语。所以生成式 AI 的基础让我们能够生成内部思想：思考、推理、逐步推理、解决问题。它还让我们能做另一件现在非常重要的事，就是生成智能来控制其他东西。生成控制来使用工具。明白吗？使用浏览器、电子表格、Photoshop、PowerPoint，使用 AutoCAD，使用其他工具。现在，这些工具是数字的，但有一天会是机械的。所以如果我向一个机械系统生成指令，那就叫机器人。如果我向一个有方向盘的机器生成指令，那就叫自动驾驶汽车。明白吗？所以两年前，事实上，你看到的基础就是我们称之为 ChatGPT 的东西，大家都说：“挺好玩的，有点傻。”或者生成了大量胡言乱语。这都不假，但它是带来所有这一切的基础技术。两年后，我们现在有了智能体系统。这是看待 AI 的一种视角。我刚刚描述的就是 AI 能做什么的视角。

turns.en: And so now all of you realize, you see it from ChatGPT, you see it from Codex, you see it from Claude Code, you see that it's now able to not just understand, but it's able to do work. Reason and do work. Now, 2 years ago when AI was able to understand you and generate information that was interesting, novel, a little cute, whenever you need a poem written, great way to do it, right? Who doesn't want to write a country song? And so that was 2 years ago, but now because it's able to do work, AI is valuable. Valuable meaning it can generate information, it can generate useful work, and it could be paid for it. Because we pay for we're interested in having friends that are smart. We love people who are know-it-alls, but we don't pay them for it. We pay for people who do work. Does that make sense? All right. Which is what happened in the last 2 years, AI went from having this capability to now generative AI went from not very valuable to now producing useful work. So much useful work that you and I are doing this every day, we're paying AI by the hour. Right? And so we might pay them $30 an hour to do the work, $20 an hour to do the work. We're basically paying AI a lot of money today. The fastest growing software business in the history of mankind. Because now it's doing useful work and we can pay them to do it.
turns.zh: 现在你们所有人都意识到了，从 ChatGPT、Codex、Claude Code 都可以看到，AI 不仅能够理解，还能执行工作。推理并完成工作。两年前，当 AI 能够理解你并生成有趣、新奇、有点可爱的信息时，比如写首诗，那是很好的方式，对吧？谁不想写首乡村歌曲呢？那是两年前的事，但现在因为它能完成工作，AI 变得有价值了。有价值意味着它能生成信息、生成有用的工作，并且人们愿意为此付费。因为我们喜欢聪明的朋友，我们喜欢万事通，但我们不会付钱给他们。我们只付钱给做事的人。明白吗？这就是过去两年发生的事，AI 从具备这种能力到生成式 AI 从不太有价值变为现在能产生有用的工作。有用的工作如此之多，你我每天都在使用，我们按小时付费给 AI。对吧？我们可能付每小时 30 美元、20 美元让它们工作。我们今天真的在给 AI 付很多钱。这是人类历史上增长最快的软件业务。因为它现在能做有用的工作，我们愿意为此付费。

turns.en: Now, that's one view of AI, which is what it can do. But one other view of AI that's really important to help reason through what Constantine is saying. So for example, the reason why some companies some people are able to build great businesses and could maneuver themselves into the center of very large industries is because when they see this capability, this is interesting. One interesting thought is if we're able to do this, what is the implication to the downstream industries? That's an interesting conversation we should have. Okay? So, now that AI can do this, what happens to all the industries like health care and financial services and life sciences, manufacturing, logistics, transportation, on and on and on. E-tail, advertising, future entertainment, the list the list of conversations you can have about now that AI can do this, what can it do as a result subsequently? That's an interesting conversation, but you should go upstream, meaning industrially, what does that mean? And so, the first thing you realize is this. Go back to first principles. I had told you just now that AI is software and it's being produced by a computer. Now, what happened to the computer that has made it possible to do this? Well, the big idea is about if you think about the computers as we know it today, really emerged about 64 years ago. IBM System/360 was the biggest announcement of computing and 64 years ago, IBM was the most valuable company in the world. Okay? And they created the modern understanding of computers. Everything that we can describe about computer was really described in 1964. For 60 for 40 years, largely has remained the same. And what happened was what happened was that that form of computing is called pre-recorded. You write down your story, you save it to a file. You write a program by hand, you save it to a file. You take a picture, you save it to a file, you record music, you save it to a file, you make a video. Right now, we're in the streaming right now, but somebody's going to record it, you're going to save it to a file. And when you want to use it later, you retrieve it from the disk drive. Does that make sense? And the retrieval process is done intelligently. So, that's why everybody's retrieval of a news story is a little bit different. It's called a recommender system.
turns.zh: 这是 AI 的一种视角，即它能做什么。但还有另一种非常重要的视角，帮助思考 Constantine 所说的。例如，为什么有些公司、有些人能够创建伟大的企业并使自己处于巨大行业的中心，是因为当他们看到这种能力时，会想：如果我们能做到这个，对下游行业意味着什么？这是一个值得讨论的有趣话题。现在 AI 能做到这些了，医疗、金融服务、生命科学、制造、物流、交通等等行业会发生什么？电子商务、广告、未来娱乐，相关的讨论清单很长。但你应该向上游思考，从产业角度，这意味着什么？所以，你首先意识到的是：回到第一性原理。我刚才说过，AI 是软件，由计算机产生。那么计算机发生了什么变化才使这一切成为可能？核心在于，我们今天所知道的计算机，实际上大约出现在 64 年前。IBM System/360 是计算机史上最重大的发布，64 年前，IBM 是全球市值最高的公司。他们创建了现代计算机的概念。我们所能描述的有关计算机的一切，实际上在 1964 年就已描述完毕。此后的四五十年间，基本保持不变。这种计算形式我称之为预记录模式。你写下故事，保存到文件；手写程序，保存到文件；拍张照片，保存到文件；录制音乐，保存到文件；制作视频，保存到文件。现在我们在直播，但有人会录制并保存到文件。以后想使用时，从磁盘中检索出来。明白吗？检索过程是智能实现的，所以每个人获取新闻故事的方式会略有不同，这叫推荐系统。

transcript.secZh: 上游影响：重新思考计算

turns.en: But basically, computers as we know it today is a retrieval-based system, which is the reason why these buildings are called data centers. They store data. Notice they don't call them computer centers, because they're not doing much computing. They just store data that you retrieve based on what you touch on your phone. Now, in order for this AI to work as I described, every time I say something to it, I have to give it new information—we call it context. I give it a new prompt, which is called a query. Between the context and the query, it will understand it first, reason about it, and produce an output based on that context and that query. Based on the circumstance. Does that make sense so far? Okay, give me one nod. Okay?
turns.zh: 从根本上说，我们今天所知的计算机是一个基于检索的系统，这就是为什么这些建筑被称为数据中心。它们存储数据。注意，他们不叫它计算机中心，因为没做太多计算。它们只是存储数据，你根据在手机上触摸的内容来检索。现在，为了让这个 AI 像我描述的那样工作，每次我对它说话时，都必须给它新信息——我们称之为上下文。我给它一个新提示，那叫一个查询。在上下文和查询之间，它会先理解，进行推理，然后基于那个上下文和查询产生一个输出。基于具体情况。到目前为止有道理吗？好，给我点个头。好。

turns.en: And so, if that is the case, every time you use the AI, the content is produced originally every single time. Everything I'm saying to you right now is being produced in real time. And it's because my explanation is based on the fact that I realize all of you have come from 60 different countries, 128 different families. You all have many different backgrounds. Some of you probably came from the computer industry. Most of you probably did not. And so, I'm explaining the information to you in a way that is sufficiently deep, but ultimately my goal is this: so that you know how to make your next investment. That's what I'm leading to. And so, I'm going to give you enough sufficient information that you can reason about it for yourself, so that when you see something in the future, you go, 'That's worth investing in. That's going to be a big industry. That's $100 billion right now, and it looks really big, but that's nothing compared to how big it's going to be.' I'm going to give you the intuition to solve that problem, okay?
turns.zh: 那么，如果是这样的话，每次你使用 AI，内容都是每次全新生成的。我现在对你说的每一句话都是实时产生的。这是因为我的解释基于一个事实：我意识到你们来自 60 个不同的国家、128 个不同的家庭。你们都有着不同的背景。你们中有些人可能来自计算机行业，大多数人可能不是。所以，我正在以足够深入的方式向你们解释这些信息，但最终我的目标是：让你们知道如何进行下一次投资。那才是我要引向的。所以，我会给你们足够充分的信息，让你们自己能够推理，这样将来当你们看到什么东西时，你们会说，‘那值得投资，那会是一个巨大的产业。现在它值 1000 亿美元，看起来已经很大了，但与它未来的规模相比根本不算什么。’我会给你们解决那个问题的直觉，好吗？

turns.en: And so here we are. We went from a computer industry that was largely based on retrieval for 60 years, and all of a sudden one day it's completely generated in real time. We call it intelligence. This is what I'm doing right now for you. I'm demonstrating intelligence. Contextual awareness, he gave me a prompt, and here comes my answer. Does it make sense?
turns.zh: 于是我们就到了这里。我们从一个 60 年来主要基于检索的计算机行业，突然有一天完全变成了实时生成。我们称之为智能。这就是我现在正在为你们做的。我在演示智能。情境意识，他给了我一个提示，于是我的回答就来了。有道理吗？

turns.en: Artificial intelligence.
turns.zh: 人工智能。

turns.en: Extremely artificial intelligence, okay?
turns.zh: 极其人工智能，好吗？

turns.en: And so here's what's going on now. I just gave you one word earlier: generative AI. The computer of today has been completely reinvented—it's now generative. And every single letter you see, every single word you see in the future, every video, every image, every ad, every TV commercial, every single time you read a story, a news story—every one of them will be different. What Constantine sees, what I see, what you see will be completely different because it'll be generated for you. Because your interest, your context, who you are, for what reason you asked, how you asked is completely different. Does it make sense?
turns.zh: 那么现在的情况是这样的。我之前只给了你们一个词：生成式 AI。今天的计算机已经被彻底重新发明了——它现在是生成式的。你未来看到的每一个字母、每一个单词、每一个视频、每一张图片、每一个广告、每一个电视广告、你每次读到一个故事、一篇新报道——每一个都会是不同的。康斯坦丁看到的、我看到的、你看到的，将会完全不同，因为它会为你生成。因为你的兴趣、你的上下文、你是谁、你问的原因、你问的方式，全都是完全不同的。有道理吗？

turns.en: And therefore, every single pixel that you see, every single sound that you hear in the future, every video you see in the future will be originally generated, not retrieved. Which means in the future we need a lot more generators. And these generators are what we build. That's what we build for a living. These are large computers, and they're generating intelligence.
turns.zh: 因此，你未来看到的每一个像素、听到的每一个声音、看到的每一个视频，都将是最初生成的，而不是检索来的。这意味着未来我们需要多得多的生成器。而这些生成器正是我们制造的东西。那就是我们赖以生存的事业。这些是大型计算机，它们在生成智能。

turns.en: Now the next question is: How big could it be? Well, it turns out the amount of information, the amount of generation of intelligence—we do it for about a billion people in the world today. Now that I told you that AI has become agentic, meaning that it can actually do work by itself. Well, if it can do work by itself, then one agent can communicate with another agent and say, 'I have some work to do. Let's team up together, and let's do some work.' And now you have all these different agents, and they're all working together to solve problems inside your company, say. So, inside our company, Constantine knows that we are huge users of agentic AI. We have hundreds of thousands of agents probably running around right now that are doing work, and they're talking to each other, and they're solving problems. All guard railed, all sandboxed—guard railed and sandboxed—but they're all working with each other. Which means in the future, it is very likely that the internet that we use today for a billion people will likely mostly be several billion, call it a hundred billion agents working around the clock, and they're using the internet and talking to each other. And what are they saying? So, for example, there'll be companies working with companies, employees' agents working with other employees' agents, there'll be self-driving cars, which are agentic, there'll be robots, which are agentic, all the manufacturing systems, every building will be agentic, there'll be agents all over the place, and they'll be using the internet, and all of those commands that they generate to each other will be generated, all of the thoughts that they have to understand—all generated. Does that make sense?
turns.zh: 那么下一个问题是：它能有多大？结果是，信息的量，智能生成的总量——我们今天为全球大约 10 亿人做这件事。现在，我告诉过你们 AI 已经变得具有代理性，意味着它可以自己完成工作。那么，如果它能自己工作，一个代理就可以与另一个代理沟通，说：‘我有一些工作要做。咱们组队，一起干些活。’于是你有了所有这些不同的代理，它们都在共同努力解决你公司内部的问题。在我们公司里，康斯坦丁知道，我们是代理式 AI 的重度用户。我们很可能有数十万个代理在运行，做着工作，它们互相交谈，解决问题。全部有护栏，全部在沙盒中——有护栏、在沙盒中——但它们都在彼此协作。这意味着在未来，我们今天为 10 亿人使用的互联网，很可能主要是由几十亿，比方说 1000 亿个代理昼夜不停地工作，它们在使用互联网并相互交谈。它们都在说些什么呢？例如，将有公司与公司合作，员工代理与其他员工代理合作，将有自动驾驶汽车，它们是代理式的，将有机器人，也是代理式的，所有制造系统，每栋建筑都将是代理式的，代理将无处不在，它们将使用互联网，而它们彼此生成的所有命令都将是被生成的，它们需要理解的所有思想——全都是生成的。有道理吗？

transcript.sec: A Layer of Intelligence Cocooning the Earth

turns.en: And so, basically, the world is going to be this layer of computing that's going to cocoon the earth, and it's going to be generating intelligence all the time. Now, I just said something that sounds ridiculous, except in fact, it's already happened.
turns.zh: 所以，从根本上说，世界将变成这一层计算，它将包裹地球，并且会不停地生成智能。我刚说了一些听起来很荒谬的话，但事实上，它已经发生过了。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Twice.
turns.zh: 两次。

turns.en: So, 300 years ago a company in Germany called Siemens produced a machine. And this machine is a really interesting machine. You go up to this machine, you light it on fire, and then this incredible invisible force comes out the other end. Nobody understood what it was. We understand it now as electricity. How many power generators are there in the world? We call it a grid. Power generation cocoons the planet. We call it the grid. And then, of course, 20-some-odd years ago—earlier than that, 35 years ago—this networking scheme, this networking matrix fabric was created here in the United States, eventually became the internet. And where is it? It cocoons the world. And so now you have energy, communications, intelligence, and it will cocoon the world. And we'll use it for, you know, it'll just be a commodity and we'll use it all over the place.
turns.zh: 那么，300 年前，德国一家叫西门子的公司制造了一台机器。这台机器非常有趣。你走到这台机器前，把它点燃，然后这种不可思议的隐形力量就从另一端出来了。当时没有人明白它是什么。我们现在知道那是电。世界上有多少台发电机？我们称之为电网。发电包裹着地球。我们称之为电网。然后，当然，二十几年前——比那更早，35 年前——这个网络方案，这个网络矩阵结构，是在美国这里创造出来的，最终成了互联网。而它在哪里？它包裹着世界。所以现在你拥有了能源、通信、智能，它将包裹世界。我们会用它，你知道，它只会成为一种商品，我们将到处使用它。

turns.en: And so what Nvidia does for a living is this new machine. The machine that was invented 300 years ago—that dynamo—anything that moves comes in, could be waterfalls, it could be wind, fire, steam, transfer it from motion—atoms, right?—to electrons. Atoms to electrons. We then take the electrons into our machine called Nvidia. Electrons now come into our machine, come into this factory, and what comes out are numbers. These numbers, depending on how you combine them, turn into language, math, it can also turn into a new language we've learned: proteins, we learned the language of human biology. We learned the language of the physical world, physics, climate, weather.
turns.zh: 那么，Nvidia 赖以生存的就是这种新机器。300 年前发明的那台机器——那个发电机——任何运动的东西都进来，可以是瀑布、可以是风、火、蒸汽，把它从运动——原子，对吧？——转换成电子。原子到电子。然后我们把电子送进我们这台叫 Nvidia 的机器。电子现在进入我们的机器，进入这个工厂，出来的则是数字。这些数字，根据你如何组合，变成语言、数学，还可以变成我们已经学会的新语言：蛋白质，我们学会了人类生物学的语言。我们学会了物理世界的语言，物理、气候、天气。

turns.en: The amount of safety and guardrails, and grounding of truth, the technology has advanced so fast to make it safe. I am certain I can tell you this completely with fact. I prefer my car today than the car that was 100 years ago. The technology is a lot better, but it's a lot safer. And it takes a lot of technology to be invented in order for it to be safe. And so, I can tell you that it is our job, it is the responsibility of the industries, and the responsibility of scientists and engineers for us to build AI safely. Two, it is your responsibility to make sure that you tell the people that you love whether it's your family, your kids, your grandkids, or the company you work for, or the country that you're in. Whatever we do, engage AI. If we think it's a superpower, engage it. Because if we don't engage it, somebody else will. We're not going to lose our lives to AI. We're going to lose our lives to somebody who uses AI. And so that's my point.
turns.zh: 在安全、护栏和事实基础的保障方面，技术进步之快已使 AI 变得安全。我可以完全肯定地告诉你这一点。我更喜欢我现在的汽车，而不是 100 年前的汽车。技术先进得多，但也安全得多。要达到这种安全水平，需要发明许多技术。所以，我可以告诉你，构建安全的 AI 是我们的工作，是产业界的责任，也是科学家和工程师的责任。第二，你有责任确保你告诉你所爱的人——无论是你的家人、孩子、孙辈，还是你所在的公司或国家——无论我们做什么，都要使用 AI。如果认为 AI 是一种超能力，就去使用它。因为如果我们不用，别人也会用。我们不会因为 AI 而失去生计，我们会因为使用 AI 的人而失去生计。所以这就是我的观点。

turns.en: That's too serious.
turns.zh: 那太严肃了。

turns.en: That was because he said the word job. So I've got a trigger, and the trigger is a bunch of people making stuff up about jobs.
turns.zh: 那是因为他提到了“工作”这个词。所以我有一个触发点，这个触发点就是有一群人总在编造关于工作的胡话。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: We put a trillion dollars into the world's ecosystem this year, did we not? What's it doing? Making jobs. Right now, the energy sector, more jobs than ever. The chip sector, more jobs than ever. Infrastructure layer, more jobs than ever. Everything from land, power, shell, finances. AI model layer, more jobs than ever. And we just said a hundred billion dollars last year went into the upper layer, more jobs than ever. We're creating so many more jobs.
turns.zh: 我们今年向全球生态系统投入了一万亿美元，不是吗？它在做什么？在创造工作。眼下，能源行业的工作岗位比以往任何时候都多。芯片行业、基础设施层的工作机会也创下新高。从土地、电力、壳牌到金融，一切都在增长。AI 模型层的工作也空前增多。我们刚提到去年有一千亿美元流向了上层应用，工作机会也比以往任何时候都多。我们正在创造如此多的就业。

transcript.sec: Jobs vs tasks: the CEO example

turns.en: Now somebody might say, "Well, what about the traditional jobs?" So let me give you the example. You know that everybody's job and their task is related, not the same. A job and the task you do in the job is related, not the same. So for example, my job is to be the CEO, to lead the company. Most of the time, and I spent a lot of it today, most of my time, my task is typing and talking.
turns.zh: 现在有人可能会说：“那传统工作呢？”让我给你举个例子。要知道，每个人的工作和他们做的任务是相关的，但不是一回事。一份工作和你在这份工作中所做的任务，是相关的，但并不等同。比如，我的工作是担任 CEO，领导公司。大部分时间——我今天就花了很多时间——我大部分时间做的任务是打字和讲话。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And so you could say CEO equals typing and talking. Both of them, AI does in a superhuman way. And I'm busier than ever.
turns.zh: 所以你可以说 CEO 就等于打字和讲话。这两件事，AI 都能以超人的水平完成。而我却比以往任何时候都更忙。

transcript.sec: The radiology example: AI augments, not eliminates

turns.en: Now, of course that's a really cute example, but let me give you a more deep example and you can now apply it. So, slightly more than 10 years ago, one of the world's leading computer scientists wanted to warn everybody about the power of AI. And so he said, and Constantine probably knows who it is, he said the first job that AI will destroy and eliminate and I advise nobody goes into this field because this field will be wiped out
turns.zh: 当然，那是个很讨巧的例子，但让我给你一个更深刻的例子，你就能活学活用。大约十多年前，一位世界顶尖的计算机科学家想提醒大家警惕 AI 的力量。他说——康斯坦丁大概知道是谁——他说 AI 会首先摧毁并消灭一种职业，他建议谁都别进入这个领域，因为它会被彻底消灭——

turns.en: Radiology.
turns.zh: 放射科。

turns.en: Is radiology. Computer vision is superhuman already 12 years ago. A computer can recognize images, detect anomalies with superhuman capability, never gets tired, never misses a detail. 12 years ago it was able to do that and he predicted as a result of that radiology is going to be wiped out. Well, he was absolutely right. Radiology was completely penetrated by computer vision. Computer vision proliferated through every single form of radiology and every radiology staff and every radiologist today is augmented by computer vision. However, the interesting thing is this: radiology demand went up. The number of radiologists in the world went up. Why? Audience participation, please. Why? I heard some of the things that it's all true. It turns out radiology spends a lot of time studying scans. But the purpose of the radiologist is to work with doctors to diagnose disease. To work with doctors to diagnose disease. And because it's now automated, they are more productive. So, two things happen. More patients are admitted into the hospital. They do more scans. The radiology department became more profitable. When they realized they were more profitable and they were admitting more patients, they hired more radiologists so that they could admit more patients so that they could make more money, take care of more people because as it turns out, there are a lot of people who are suffering and they were waiting to get into the hospital. So, now let's pretend for a second. Do you appreciate the computer scientist tell you it's going to be the end of the world for radiologists? My point is we have to be responsible about what we make up because we could have done harm. And it turns out the number of people who want to be radiologists after his speech because it permeated through everything, the number of radiologists started to decline. But we need more radiologists.
turns.zh: 就是放射科。计算机视觉早在 12 年前就已经是超人水平了。计算机能够以超人的能力识别图像、检测异常，永不疲劳，从不遗漏细节。12 年前它就能做到这些，于是他预测放射科将因此被消灭。嗯，他完全正确：放射科确实被计算机视觉全面渗透了。计算机视觉普及到放射科的每一种形式，如今每位放射科医生和放射科工作人员都得到了计算机视觉的增强。然而有趣的是，对放射科的需求反而增加了。全球的放射科医生数量也增加了。为什么？请观众参与，为什么？我听到了一些说法，都对。原来放射科医生花大量时间研究扫描影像，但放射科医生的真正目的是与医生合作诊断疾病。与医生合作诊断疾病。因为这现在自动化了，他们的效率更高了。于是两件事发生了：更多患者入院，做了更多扫描，放射科变得更赚钱。当他们意识到自己更赚钱且能接更多患者时，就雇了更多放射科医生，以便能接更多患者，赚更多钱，治疗更多人——因为事实上有大量患者正饱受痛苦，在医院外等待。现在，我们想一下，你欣赏那位计算机科学家告诉你放射科医生要完蛋吗？我的意思是，我们必须对自己编造的话负责，因为我们可能已经造成了伤害。事实上，在那次演讲之后，因为那些话传遍了，想当放射科医生的人开始减少。但我们需要更多的放射科医生。

transcript.secZh: 放射学案例：AI增强而非取代

transcript.sec: Software engineers: solving problems, not coding

turns.en: Now, somebody recently said 90% of software coding will be gone and therefore we don't need software engineers. Meanwhile, we're hiring more software engineers than ever. And the reason for that is because a software engineer's job is to solve problems and dream up problems to solve, innovate. I never hired somebody and said, "Hey, guess what? You're a software engineer. Listen, here's a keyboard. Show me how many words a second you can type." Typing is not the job of a software engineer. Coding is not their job. Solving problems is their job.
turns.zh: 最近有人说，90% 的软件编写工作将消失，所以我们不再需要软件工程师。然而，我们雇用的软件工程师比以往任何时候都多。原因是，软件工程师的工作是解决问题、构想值得解决的问题、进行创新。我雇人时从不会说：“嘿，你是软件工程师。来，这是键盘，让我看看你每秒能敲多少个字。”打字不是软件工程师的工作。写代码也不是他们的工作。解决问题才是他们的工作。

transcript.secZh: 软件工程师：解决问题而非编码

turns.en: And so, I just gave you two examples. Task versus purpose. Does that make sense? It turns out this example happens all over the place. But because we have such a contrived, such a naive understanding that computer scientists could say things like 50% of the jobs will be gone. Software coding is completely irrelevant. Radiology is going to be wiped out because we think about it from the task perspective. We forgot the purpose of the job.
turns.zh: 所以，我刚刚给了你们两个例子。任务 vs 目的。这有道理吗？这样的例子比比皆是。但我们有一种矫揉造作、天真幼稚的理解，让计算机科学家能说出 50% 的工作会消失、软件编写完全无关紧要、放射科会被消灭之类的话，因为我们只从任务的角度看问题。我们忘记了工作的目的。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

transcript.sec: AI elevates jobs, doesn't eliminate them

turns.en: There were radiologists before there were workstations. There're going to be radiologists after AI. There were engineers before software coding. I promise you that. There will be engineers after. Does that make sense? And so, that's the way to think about jobs. And I've now covered two things. One, if your country is not investing in AI, there's a massive boom of jobs that you're missing out on. If your country or your company is not investing in AI, there's a level of elevation of your people that you're missing out on. AI is not going to eliminate jobs. AI is going to elevate your job. If I were a plumber today, largely, I get a job task sheet or a schematic. However, if I'm a plumber tomorrow, it is very likely I'm a designer as well.
turns.zh: 在影像工作站出现之前就有放射科医生。AI 出现之后仍然会有。在软件编码出现之前就有工程师。我向你保证，之后仍然会有。有道理吗？所以，这才是思考工作的方式。我现在讲了两点。第一，如果你的国家不投资 AI，你就会错失巨大的就业浪潮。如果你的国家或公司不投资 AI，你就会错失提升员工的机会。AI 不会消灭工作，AI 会提升你的工作。如果我今天是水管工，我主要拿到的是任务单或图纸。但如果我明天还是水管工，我很可能同时也是一位设计师。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Does that make sense? Because you and I both know
turns.zh: 有道理吗？因为你我都知道——

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: that we could just use AI to generate decent, incredible designs of a kitchen if I'm a carpenter.
turns.zh: 如果我是个木匠，我们完全可以利用 AI 生成美观绝伦的厨房设计。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: If I were a salesperson of furniture, I'm going to be an interior designer for sure.
turns.zh: 如果我是一个家具销售员，我肯定会变成室内设计师。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And so, I've elevated my craft. Went from somebody who sells furniture to somebody who could advise you on how beautiful your home could be. I went from somebody who's a carpenter.
turns.zh: 这样，我就提升了我的手艺。从一个卖家具的人，变成能为你建议怎样让家更美的人。从一个木匠，变成能为你设计梦想厨房的人。

turns.en: You're expecting me to come and just put some wood together. And now I'm your home designer. You've elevated my craft, I've given you so many examples, but that's my point. I think the narrative about AI is absolutely wrong. The goal is to scare everybody out of it so that some people could benefit from it. But AI, as you know, is the greatest force for eliminating the technology divide in my entire career. I spent 40-some years. My entire life has been computer design. This entire time the technology we created became more and more complex, and the number of people who could program these computers as a percentage of population declined. Who in this room knows C++? Come on, cut it out, you weirdos. This row, is it a startup company? Okay. So we're looking at 2%. 2% and this is a very strange room. So 2% of society knows C++. How many people know human? More than 2%. And so everybody now can program a computer, and yet in the past only 2% could. We have closed the technology divide. We've got to bring everybody with us. Does that make sense? Anyway, that's it. On a Friday night that's too serious.
turns.zh: 你原本只是期待我来把几块木头拼到一起，现在我却成了你的家居设计师。我的技艺提升了，我给了你这么多例子，但这就是我的观点。我认为关于 AI 的叙事完全错了。其目的是吓跑所有人，以便让某些人从中受益。但你知道，AI 是我职业生涯中消除技术鸿沟的最强大力量。我花了 40 多年时间。我毕生都在做计算机设计。这 40 多年里，我们创造的技术变得越来越复杂，能够编程这些计算机的人数占总人口的比例在下降。在座的有谁懂 C++？得了吧，别装了，你们这些怪胎。这一排是初创公司吗？好吧。所以我们看到大概 2%。2%，这个房间已经很不寻常了。那么，社会上只有 2% 的人懂 C++。有多少人懂人类语言？多于 2%。因此，现在每个人都能给计算机编程，而在过去只有 2% 的人能做到。我们消除了技术鸿沟。我们必须带上所有人。这说得通吧？好了，周五晚上聊这些太严肃了。

turns.en: That is extremely optimistic and I agree. It's great to hear from someone who is closer to actual building of the actual technology that powers everything than anyone else in the world. So Jensen, you talked about a future where we move from retrieval, this paradigm that we've had our entire lives, to generation where everything is customized, knowledge is customized for the individual. A world where we have the generation of intelligence, paralleling from the energy to the telecommunications revolution to now the intelligence revolution. You talked about these languages that the computer can speak, not just English or German, but even protein. You talked about five layers of participation, abundant opportunity to participate in this revolution for everyone in this room and everyone listening. And you talked about how this transformation is going to have real consequences that allow people to move from just doing the task to dreaming the problems and the solutions, maybe even a life of purpose, a life where we move from carpenters to architects. Thank you, Jensen. Please join me in thanking Jensen Huang, the man who made this all happen.
turns.zh: 这极其乐观，我完全同意。能听到真正在打造这一切核心技术的、比世界上任何人都更接近技术实际构建的人这样讲，真是太好了。Jensen，你谈到了一个未来，我们从检索这个我们整个人生都习以为常的范式，转向生成——一切都个性化，知识为个人定制。一个智能生成的世界，与能源、电信革命并驾齐驱，直至现在这场智能革命。你谈到了计算机能说的语言，不只是英语或德语，甚至包括蛋白质。你谈到了五个参与层次，在座的以及所有听众都能获得参与这场革命的丰厚机会。你还谈到这场转型将带来真正的深远影响，让人们从仅仅执行任务，走向构想问题和解决方案，甚至获得一种有目标的人生，一种从木匠转变为建筑师的人生。谢谢你，Jensen。请和我一起感谢让这一切成为现实的人，Jensen Huang。

turns.en: Thank you. Thank you so much.
turns.zh: 谢谢，非常感谢。

turns.en: You're welcome.
turns.zh: 不客气。

tldr.en: AI evolved from generative chatbots to agentic systems that reason and do useful work.
tldr.zh: AI 已从生成式聊天机器人演变为能推理并做有用工作的代理系统。

tldr.en: AI factories—massive GPU clusters—produce intelligence tokens, representing a multi-trillion-dollar investment opportunity.
tldr.zh: AI 工厂——大规模 GPU 集群——生产智能代币，代表数万亿美元的投资机会。

tldr.en: AI won't eliminate jobs; it elevates them by automating tasks, letting people focus on purpose.
tldr.zh: AI 不会消灭工作；它通过自动化任务来提升工作，让人们专注于目的。

qs.en: Will AI lead to job losses?
What is the difference between tasks and purpose?
